_note:
Slots for [brg_our-restaurants-brands]. Declared beside the fragment so a slot and its {token} ship in one commit. Generated into website/acf/ by `python3 kit/build-acf.py`; never hand-edit an acf.json. Slot names are underscore-only. Defaults are esc_html'd on fill, so write literal characters — a literal `&` and a literal `—`, never `&` or `—`.

Slots are NAMED PER BRAND (`bnb_*`, `odies_*`), deliberately not numbered `brand_1_*`/`brand_2_*`. Numbering would imply a repeater whose length is content, and it isn't: each plate carries its own brand lockup artwork, so a third brand is a BUILD task (new asset, new plate) rather than a content edit. Naming them says that. Same reasoning as home-about's vision/mission — two named things, not two rows.

The brand lockup plates deliberately have NO image reveal: the 2->1.2 counter-scale was cropping the wordmarks, and a brand mark should not be cropped for an effect (2026-08-10). They keep a plain fade-up, and that stays as code.

_baseline.why: Sean 2026-08-13 ruled the canonical name carries the Co. — odies_heading went from Odie's Pizza to Odie's Pizza Co. A deliberate approved copy change, verified rendering on one line.

bnb_heading.label: Board & Brew — name
bnb_heading.doc: The brand name. Write `&` as a literal ampersand.

bnb_body_1.label: Board & Brew — first paragraph
bnb_body_1.default: San Diego's iconic sandwich shop. Board & Brew has been handcrafting sandos with fresh-baked bread and premium ingredients since before craft sandwiches were cool.

bnb_body_2.label: Board & Brew — second paragraph
bnb_body_2.doc: Carries the live location count, so it needs editing whenever that changes. Write `—` as a literal em dash. CROSS-SECTION FACT — this number also appears in `home-community` -> Body copy second paragraph, and `community-stats` -> Stat 1 figure. Going ACF-editable REMOVED the check that used to catch a mismatch: it was three greppable strings in the repo, and it is now three database rows that nothing repo-side can compare. If you change one, change all three. (`doc` strings are per-field by construction, so this warning has to be repeated in each — there is nowhere on this project that can hold a cross-section fact.)
bnb_body_2.default: 12 locations across San Diego and Orange County — each one a neighborhood staple.

bnb_cta_href.label: Board & Brew — button link
bnb_cta_href.doc: Opens in a new tab; target/rel are in the markup.

odies_heading.label: Odie's — name
odies_heading.doc: The brand name. CANONICAL FORM — Sean 2026-08-13: the official name carries the Co. at the end. Body copy is deliberately NOT swept to match; he asked that prose follow whatever copy is provided, and both forms are in use interchangeably. So this field is the one place the official name is asserted — change it here, leave the paragraphs alone.

odies_body_1.label: Odie's — first paragraph
odies_body_1.doc: Write `—` as a literal em dash.
odies_body_1.default: Oceanside's newest pizza obsession. Odie's Pizza Co. brings sourdough pies and radical vibes to the Southern California coast — think big slices, bold flavors, and a neighborhood vibe that makes you want to stick around.

odies_body_2.label: Odie's — second paragraph
odies_body_2.doc: Says more locations are coming, so it will need editing when they land.
odies_body_2.default: Our flagship is right in the heart of downtown Oceanside, and more locations are on the way.

odies_cta_href.label: Odie's — button link
odies_cta_href.doc: Opens in a new tab; target/rel are in the markup.

bnb_image.label: Board & Brew — image
bnb_image.doc: The artwork in the Board & Brew panel. Landscape, around 800x550. An SVG logo lockup or a photo both work. Leave empty to keep the current picture.

bnb_image_tone.label: Board & Brew — image — color
bnb_image_tone.doc: Color is the default. Switch this photo to black and white when you want it that way on purpose — the photography on this site was only ever gray because the placeholder images were. Affects this photo alone.

bnb_image_px.label: Board & Brew — image — movement
bnb_image_px.doc: How far this photo drifts inside its frame as you scroll, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off. The dropdown this replaces offered 6, 10 and 16 as Subtle, Medium and Strong, so anything already set still reads exactly the same — you can now pick the values in between. 40 is the ceiling: the page itself stops there, so a larger number would do nothing. The photo is laid out taller than its frame and slides within it, so an edge never appears and it is never zoomed.

bnb_image_px_dir.label: Board & Brew — image — movement direction
bnb_image_px_dir.doc: Which way this photo travels as the page scrolls. Neighboring photos set in opposite directions are what reads as depth.

bnb_image_float.label: Board & Brew — image — frame drift
bnb_image_float.doc: Moves the whole frame across the section, on top of the movement inside it, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off; 8 and 12 were the old Gentle and Strong. 40 is the ceiling. Leave this off for a photo that fills its section edge to edge — there is nothing behind it to reveal.

bnb_image_float_dir.label: Board & Brew — image — drift direction
bnb_image_float_dir.doc: Which way this frame drifts. Set a large and a small photo in opposite directions.
